hints: Focus on how addition polymerisation works, the C=C double bond opens up to make two new C-C single bonds in the backbone.
Notice the polymer backbone has Cl atoms attached directly to it, so the monomer must have Cl attached directly to the C=C carbons.
Look at the middle -CH2-CH2- link where two monomer units join, and work backwards to split the 4-carbon section into two identical 2-carbon alkenes.
walkthrough:
**Recall addition polymerisation**

Remember that an alkene monomer adds to the chain by breaking its pi bond. A $C=C$ becomes $-C-C-$ in the polymer backbone.

$$ \text{monomer: } C=C \rightarrow \text{polymer: } -C-C- $$

**Analyse the section shown**

Look closely at the backbone. It is four carbons long: $-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})-$

The Cl atoms are bonded directly to backbone carbons, not in a side chain. So the monomer must be a substituted ethene with Cl on the double bond.

**Split into two monomers**

Split the section in the middle between the two $\text{CH}_2$ groups. Each half is $-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-$, which comes from $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$.

$$ 2\, \text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl} \rightarrow -\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}- $$
This is a tail to tail join of two chloroethene molecules, which can occur in the chain.

options.A: CH2CHCH2Cl is 3-chloroprop-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$. Its polymer would have a $-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ side chain on every repeat unit, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{Cl})-$. The diagram shows Cl attached directly to the backbone, not via a CH2 group, so this is wrong.
options.B: CH2CHCl is chloroethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$. Opening the double bond gives the repeat unit $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$. Two of these units joined in opposite orientations give $-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$, exactly the section shown.
options.C: CH3CHCHCl is 1-chloroprop-1-ene, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CHCl}$. Its polymer would have 3 carbons per monomer and a methyl side chain, $-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHCl}-$. The section shown has no methyl branches and has only 2 carbons per monomer unit.
options.D: CHClCHCH2CH2Cl is a 4-carbon dichloroalkene, e.g. $\text{CHCl}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$. Its polymer would give a $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ side chain on the backbone. The diagram shows a straight 4-carbon backbone with no such side chain, so this cannot fit.
